key_insight: Healthcare agents perform better when the runtime harness is designed for healthcare workflows, not just terminal task completion.
clinical_relevance: A healthcare-specific harness can improve reliability, auditability, and safety checks when agents interact with EHRs, FHIR data, and clinical tools.
method: Defined the Medical Harness Protocol to score seven healthcare process dimensions.
Built MedHarnessBench with 342 executable healthcare tasks across EHR/FHIR, admin, and multimodal tools.
Compared MedHarness with general-purpose harnesses and tested single-fault perturbations to probe failure sensitivity.
evidence_signal: The study reports more than 16,000 controlled task executions showing gains in terminal success, subtask completion, and process quality.
watch_item: Results come from benchmarked executions, so real-world performance may differ depending on local workflows, tooling, and governance controls.
paper_title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation
